- [RCTS.1.2.29] **A cross-tier fixture** — a fixture in the `cross-tier`
  category ([RCTS.1.1.4]) carries `expect.engines`, an object of at least one
  member: each member's name is an engine's label, and its value an object
  of `rules_ds`, a string, that engine's program, and optionally
  `wall_clock`, the string `"unset"`. A harness must compile and load each
  program into an engine of its own, on mock clocks of its own and with a
  stream callback of its own, and must run each step on the engine its
  `engine` member, a label, names. A harness must leave the mock wall clock
  of an engine whose entry carries `wall_clock` unset, as [RCTS.1.2.32] has
  it for a logical fixture, until a `wall_set` step on that engine gives it a
  value ([LTIM.2.8.3]). Besides [RCTS.1.2.28]'s ops, a step of a cross-tier fixture may be:

  - `forward`, with `from`, a label: every fact the `from` engine published
    since the last `forward` from it to this engine ([NCBK.10.1]) is asserted
    into this engine, under its schema's name and with its slot values, in
    publication order. A harness must read the name and the values from the
    publish event while its callback runs ([NCBK.2.5]): the fact is in no
    working memory of the `from` engine ([LTIE.4.3]). Nothing else crosses
    ([NCBK.10.3]).
  - `forward_external`, with `from`, a label: every `FactExternal` the `from`
    engine's publications carried ([RFCS.23.1]), since the last
    `forward_external` from it to this engine, is given to this engine's own
    receiving interface ([NCBK.10.4]), in publication order.

  A cross-tier fixture's `expect` may carry `expected_published_asserted_at`,
  an object: each member's name is an engine's label, and its value an array
  with one entry for each fact that engine published while the steps ran, in
  publication order. The entry is the `asserted_at` of the `FactExternal` the
  publication carried ([RFCS.23.1], [RFCS.23.5]), an integer, or `null` where
  its `has_asserted_at` is false. A harness must read each from the record
  the publish event carried, and must fail the fixture when one of those
  publications carried no record, when the counts differ, or when an entry
  differs.

  A harness must fail a cross-tier fixture whose `engines` is not such an
  object, one whose `expected_published_asserted_at` is not such an object or
  names a label `engines` does not, and one with a step that carries no
  `engine`, or whose `engine` or `from` names no label. It must fail a fixture
  of any other category that carries `engines` or
  `expected_published_asserted_at`, or a step that carries `engine` or takes
  either op.
